1.title: Microsoft Sentinel
1.text: Welcome to Module nine: Microsoft Sentinel. It covers the exam area Capabilities of Microsoft security solutions. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Describe security information and event management (sim) and security orchestration automated response (soar). Describe how Microsoft Sentinel provides integrated threat protection. Describe threat detection and mitigation capabilities in Microsoft Sentinel. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Capabilities of Microsoft security solutions (thirty-five to forty percent). Exam format: forty-five minutes; a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official S C nine hundred study guide, skills measured as of October twenty-one, two thousand twenty-six.

1.title: SIEM and SOAR
1.text: sim and soar. sim. Stands for: Security information and event management. What it does: Collects and analyzes security data from many sources to detect threats. soar. Stands for: Security orchestration, automation and response. What it does: Automates responses to alerts and incidents with playbooks. Microsoft Sentinel is Microsoft's cloud-native sim and soar solution. It is built on Azure, so it scales without servers to manage, and it is now part of the Microsoft Defender portal experience.

1.title: SIEM and SOAR, continued
1.text: sim and soar. The figure shows this: Sentinel collects data, detects threats, investigates incidents and automates response. Exam tip: sim equals collect, correlate, detect. soar equals automate response. Sentinel does both. It is not an endpoint antivirus; it uses data from Defender products.

1.title: Integrated threat protection: the four jobs
1.text: Integrated threat protection: the four jobs. Collect. Data connectors bring in data from Microsoft services (Entra I D, Microsoft three sixty-five, Defender), Azure, on-premises, other clouds and third-party products. Detect. Analytics rules find threats; machine learning and User and Entity Behavior Analytics (you ee bee ay) spot unusual behavior; threat intelligence matches known bad indicators. Investigate. Incidents group related alerts; the investigation graph shows entities and relationships; hunting searches proactively. Respond. Automation rules and playbooks (built on Azure Logic Apps). Data is stored in a Log Analytics workspace and queried with Kusto Query Language. Exam tip: Sentinel ingests data through data connectors, including from Microsoft Defender products, Azure and third parties.

1.title: Threat detection and mitigation
1.text: Threat detection and mitigation. Data connectors. Ingest logs from many sources. Workbooks. Dashboards and visualizations of the data. Analytics rules. Scheduled or near-real-time queries that create alerts and incidents. Incidents. A collection of related alerts to investigate as one case. Hunting. Proactive searching with K Q L before alerts fire; bookmarks save findings. Notebooks. Use Jupyter notebooks for advanced analysis. Threat intelligence. Match logs against known malicious indicators. you ee bee ay. Baseline normal behavior to flag anomalies. Automation rules and playbooks. Respond automatically: block a user, isolate a device, open a ticket, notify a team. Content hub. Ready-made solutions: connectors, rules, workbooks, playbooks.

1.title: Threat detection and mitigation, continued
1.text: Threat detection and mitigation. The figure shows this: A Sentinel incident groups alerts from several sources and can trigger a playbook. Exam tip: Workbooks equals see. Analytics rules equals detect. Incidents equals investigate. Hunting equals look proactively. Playbooks equals automate (Logic Apps). Everything is queried with K Q L.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants one cloud-native service to collect security logs from many sources, detect threats and automate responses. Which fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Microsoft Sentinel. Sentinel is a cloud-native sim and soar.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which Sentinel feature automates a response, such as blocking a user, when an incident occurs? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Playbook. Playbooks, built on Azure Logic Apps, automate responses.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. An analyst wants to search proactively for suspicious activity before any alert fires. Which capability is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Hunting. Hunting uses queries to look for threats proactively.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. What does a Sentinel incident represent? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: A collection of related alerts to investigate together. Incidents group related alerts into one case.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Which language is used to query data in Microsoft Sentinel? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Kusto Query Language. Sentinel queries Log Analytics data with K Q L.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which term describes automating response to security alerts? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: soar. soar is security orchestration, automation and response.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What does sim stand for? Answer: Security information and event management. Question two. What does soar do? Answer: Automates responses to alerts and incidents. Question three. What brings data into Sentinel? Answer: Data connectors.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What do workbooks provide? Answer: Dashboards and visualizations. Question five. What are playbooks built on? Answer: Azure Logic Apps. Question six. Where is Sentinel data stored? Answer: In a Log Analytics workspace.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. sim and soar: collect, correlate, detect; automate response. Sentinel jobs: collect (connectors), detect (analytics, you ee bee ay, threat intelligence), investigate (incidents, hunting), respond (playbooks). Tools: workbooks, analytics rules, incidents, hunting, notebooks, content hub; K Q L; Log Analytics. In the next module, we continue the course.
